newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil quiet, notionally firmer with futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil quiet, notionally firmer with futures.

text.p: Little action was seen on the European gas oil markets on Wednesday with sellers holding off for premiums achieved earlier in the week and buyers relaxed in a balanced market, traders said.
Sellers of spot barges were steady at August IPE +$1.50 a tonne fob Rotterdam with buyers almost one dollar lower.
First half August barrels talked around August IPE +$0.75/1.50 a tonne while the second half of the month was slightly easier at August IPE +$0.5/$1.00 a tonne.
Ex-storage barrels were heard valued around August IPE +50 cents.
End-user German demand was limited and German refineries were covering the limited amount of buying with aggressively priced selling.
"It leaves little room for the importer," one seller said.

Brokers said the bottleneck at the jointly owned BP, Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam was set to continue as boats attemped to load on the 16th of the month but the refinery owners were asking those due to lift up to Friday to arrive a day or two later.
Diesel cargo premiums for prompt delivery into France were hovering around August IPE +$4.50 a tonne.
Early August barrels were slightly firmer at +$5.00 while second half of the month barrels were pegged around August IPE +$4.75 a tonne.
The influx of Russian gas oil was taking its toll and Russian gas oil premiums were falling. Some saw the market as low as parity with the IPE screen.
"It depends on the volume. If you have a 10,000 tonnes for Bremen you could get a premium of (Aug IPE) +$2.50-$3.00 but a 60Kt Russian would only get (IPE) screen flat," one cargo trader said.
Prompt 0.2 sulphur cargoes talked steady around August IPE +$1.50/2.50 a tonne.
